newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MRC hopes golf course to spur buying spree.
newsitem.headline: MRC hopes golf course to spur buying spree.

text.p: Estate developer MRC Allied Industries Inc said on Tuesday it hoped a golf course would trigger buying into its 2,266-hectare tourism flagship project.
MRC has been developing the horizontal infrastructure of Amihan Woodlands Township in Leyte, which includes a thick forest cover and a long beach, since the start of 1996.
"We already have the power, roads, telecom, water and sewerage system," chairman Benjamin Bitanga told reporters during the informal launch of the project.

The estate, which is to be marketed as "the most exclusive residential resort area in Asia", will have a marina, an airstrip, exclusive villas on the cliff, clusters of one-hectare houses, 13 beachfront resorts, a lakeside resort, three golf courses and a town centre.
The company has earmarked 30 billion pesos for the development of the estate over the next 10 years, wherein more than 800 hectares of forest area will be left untapped.
"With the launching of the golf course, the pace of development will become faster, much faster now," Bitanga said.
MRC is seeking the approval from the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell golf shares to the public.
The design of the more than 100-hectare, $14-million golf course is expected to be awarded later this week. Completion is expected after 14 to 16 months.
At least three groups, two financial institutions and a golf course developer, have expressed interest to help raise funds for the golf and country club project.
MRC was expecting net income to soar to 200 million pesos this year from 66.45 milion last year.

MRC chief operating officer Renato Leveriza said proceeds from the sale of golf shares and residential lots in Amihan and lease payment from its industrial estate in Cebu would push its revenues to 550 million pesos against 375 million last year.
